title: Fewer biased answers after model compression often coincided with more abstention
summary: On the BBQ question-answering benchmark, 20 of 26 quantization configurations with fewer biased answers also abstained more often on questions they could answer. The comparison covered models from the Qwen3, Gemma 3 and SmolLM2 families.

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 front matter, §§3–5, exact quantization comparison, prompt variation and forced-choice appendix

evidence.tested: The authors compared multiple quantization configurations and reported correct, biased, and abstaining answers separately. They also changed prompt wording and removed the abstention option in a separate comparison.
evidence.unknown: The 20-of-26 result is conditional on configurations with lower observed bias in this benchmark. It does not measure fairness in real use or establish that all compression increases abstention.
evidence.ai_role: The researchers compared outputs from Qwen3, Gemma 3 and SmolLM2 across model sizes and quantization settings, separating abstention from biased or non-biased answers.
